sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, one word or phrase, match).

questions.q: Answer in one word or phrase: (a) Why is Chandrabhan famous? (b) Name the Mughal painters of Akbar's court (any one).
questions.answer: (a) For prose and history writing in Shah Jahan's days. (b) Dasawanth, Basawan or Abd-us-Samad.
questions.note: April 2026 asked about Chandrabhan and Badayuni under languages; included here for the Mughal court context.

questions.q: Answer in two short phrases: Write any two brief characteristic features of Patachitras.
questions.answer: They are painted mostly on cloth (Orissa) and are detailed; they depict religious and mythological stories with bright colours and bold lines.

questions.q: Match two items (rest are distracters): Rangoli – North India; Alpana – Bengal; Kolam – Madhya Pradesh; Aipan – Karnataka. Give two correct pairs.
questions.answer: Rangoli – North India; Alpana – Bengal (kolam is Tamil Nadu, aipan Uttarakhand).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: Mithila paintings are made on ______ treated paper with vegetable colours and finished in ______ lines.
Fill in the blanks: Kalamkari means a painting done by ______. It is done on ______ with vegetable dyes.
Mark true or false: (a) Warli painting uses religious iconography. (b) Phad is a scroll painting.
questions.answer: (a) False – it is a secular art form. (b) True.

questions.q: Mark true or false: (a) Humayun brought two Persian painters to India. (b) Painting declined under Jahangir.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False – it reached its climax.

questions.q: Answer in a phrase: (a) Which state is famous for Phad painting? (b) Which state is famous for Kalamkari?
Answer in a phrase: (a) What was the theme of the Ajanta paintings? (b) Name two sites of Buddhist paintings of the 6th–9th centuries.
questions.answer: (a) Jataka stories and the life of the Buddha. (b) Bagh and Badami (also Sittanavasal, Ellora).

questions.q: Mark true or false: (a) Dhulicitra is painting on cloth. (b) Lepyacitra is the representation of folklore.
questions.answer: (a) False – it is painting on the floor. (b) True.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: Kalighat painting started in the early ______ century by ______ painters.
Answer in a phrase: (a) Which tribe is famous for Warli painting? (b) What material is used for the white colour?
questions.answer: (a) The Warli tribe (decorating homes of gond and kol tribes). (b) Rice paste.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in about 25 words.

questions.q: How are paintings helpful in knowing about the past?
questions.answer: Paintings show the life, customs, dress, buildings and beliefs of people of those times, how kings and courtiers dressed and sat in assembly, and so they are valuable historical records.

questions.q: Write any two brief characteristic features of Patachitras.
questions.answer: They are mostly painted on cloth and are highly detailed, similar to the Kalighat pats; they depict religious and mythological themes.

questions.q: Describe any two features of Kalighat painting.
questions.answer: It was painted on paper in water colours with clear sweeping lines, bright colours and a plain background; subjects were gods and goddesses and later social life of Bengal such as babus and courtesans.

questions.q: Mention two materials used for making Mithila paintings.
questions.answer: Vegetable colours with a few earth colours and cow-dung treated paper, finished with black lines.

questions.q: What is meant by miniature painting?
questions.answer: Small paintings on a small surface, on perishable materials like palm leaves or paper, illustrating manuscripts and themes from epics, myths, seasons (Barahmasa) and melodies (Ragamala).

questions.q: Name two features of Warli painting.
questions.answer: White rice paste on a plain background using geometric shapes and dots and crooked lines in spiralling compositions, painted by women, secular in character.

questions.q: Name two institutions set up to promote art in India.
questions.answer: The National Gallery of Modern Art and the Lalit Kala Akademi.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 40–50 words.

questions.q: Write an account of Batik paint.
questions.answer: Batik is a wax-resist dyeing and painting technique imported from the Orient and now Indianised into a mature and expensive art: wax is applied to parts of the cloth so they do not take dye, producing designs after dyeing and removing the wax.

questions.q: Describe three distinctive features of Kalamkari art.
questions.answer: It is hand painting and block printing on cloth with vegetable dyes from roots, leaves and mineral salts; subjects from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and mythology painted scene after scene with floral borders; outlines by hand-carved blocks and details with a pen of bamboo or date palm; Sri Kalahasti and Machilipatnam are centres.

questions.q: Describe the Warli painting.
questions.answer: Named after the Warli tribe of Maharashtra, it is painted by women on floors and walls using white rice paste on a plain contrasting background in geometric patterns of squares, triangles and circles with dots and crooked lines; trees, birds and daily life are shown in a spiralling composition; it is more secular than other tribal arts.

questions.q: Explain the Mithila (Madhubani) painting.
questions.answer: It is the folk art of the Mithila region of Bihar, made by village women with vegetable and earth colours and black lines on cow-dung treated paper; it shows Sita's exile, gods, sun, moon, tulsi, weddings and court scenes; it is conceptual, made for rituals, and mothers make pieces as gifts for daughters, conveying advice on married life.

questions.q: Write about the Progressive Artists Group.
questions.answer: Formed in Bombay in 1948 (1947 in the textbook for Lesson 9) under F.N. Souza with S.H. Raza, M.F. Hussain, K.H. Ara, S.K. Bakre and H.A. Gade, it broke away from the Bengal School and represented the modern forceful art of independent India.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 150–200 words.

questions.q: Describe the development of the art of painting during the medieval period.
questions.answer: Under the Delhi Sultanate murals of flowers and plants decorated palaces and mosques and Persian influence came with illustrated manuscripts. Jain merchants patronised miniature manuscripts in Gujarat and Rajasthan (14th–15th centuries) and the Palas produced palm-leaf miniatures in the east. The Mughals replaced wall painting with book illumination: Humayun brought Persian painters; Akbar encouraged portraits, cloth paintings and illustrations (Baburnama, Akbarnama) and a Persian–Indian synthesis; under Jahangir painting reached its climax with vibrant colours and depth (Mansur, Bishan Das, Manohar). Aurangzeb withdrew patronage, dispersing artists who developed Rajasthani and Pahari schools with themes from epics, Barahmasa and Ragamala.

questions.q: Explain the contribution of the Mughals to painting.
questions.answer: The Mughals began a new era by synthesising Indian painting with the Persian tradition. Humayun brought Persian painters; Akbar patronised Hindu and Persian artists, recorded their names and produced illustrated manuscripts and portraits; Jahangir, himself a connoisseur, took the art to its zenith with vibrant colours and a three-dimensional effect, while Mansur painted birds and animals; Dara Shikoh patronised painting; Mughal court painters introduced landscapes with human figures and signed miniatures.

questions.q: Describe the emergence of the Bengal School and the Progressive Artists Group.
questions.answer: After British-style art schools and Ravi Varma's oil painting, the Bengal School grew under Abanindranath and Rabindranath Tagore, E.B. Havell and Ananda Coomaraswamy at Santiniketan's Kala Bhavan, with Nandalal Bose, Binod Behari Mukherjee and Ramkinkar Baij reviving Indian themes. In 1943 the Calcutta Group depicted the people's condition. In 1948 the Progressive Artists Group of Bombay (Souza, Raza, Hussain, Ara, Bakre, Gade) broke away from the Bengal School to express the modern art of independent India; the Madras School under Roy Chowdhury and Paniker followed.

questions.q: Discuss the significance of painting as a part of culture.
questions.answer: Painting expresses the basic human need for expression from prehistoric rock art to modern art; it records the life, dress and beliefs of each age (Ajanta, Mughal miniatures, Kalighat), mixes religious and secular themes, shows the synthesis of traditions (Persian and Indian), carries folk traditions from mother to daughter (Mithila, Warli) and reflects social change and nationalism in the modern period.
